title: Priority-queue weighted SLA matcher for dedicated reserved throughput and GPU class selection
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Create a deterministic intake and prioritization mechanism for enterprise dedicated capacity requests that matches customer SLA targets to reserved throughput and GPU class using a weighted priority queue. This ticket captures the product requirements, decision trade-offs, example scoring formula, and runbook for handoffs to Capacity Operations and Engineering. Goal: reduce onboarding time and manual judgment, ensure predictable SLO alignment, and surface fallback recommendations when ideal GPU class is unavailable.
acceptance_criteria: Priority matcher prototype implemented as a decision table and example scoring function in Confluence
API for intake shows recommended reserved throughput, GPU families, and burst allowance for 90% of enterprise requests
Handbook runbook created for Capacity Ops with step-by-step escalation and override instructions
Benchmarked mapping shows expected latency/throughput delta for recommended GPU families within documented tolerance
A/B test with 10 pilot customers shows reduced intake time by >= 40% compared to manual triage
updates: 2026-03-01 - Ticket created after intake backlog review. Noted repeated manual escalations for customers asking for low-latency SLOs with high burstiness.

2026-03-03 - PM sync: collected 12 anonymized customer profiles from Sales (latency-sensitive, batch-heavy, unpredictable burst). Observed common request attributes: peak qps, P99 latency target, model family preference, compliance constraints.

2026-03-05 - Engineering (Marco Li) provided initial kernel for scoring formula: score = w1*latency_weight + w2*cost_weight + w3*burst_risk - w4*preference_penalty. Discussion: need to normalize by tokens/sec and KV cache hit rate.

2026-03-06 - Design (Rashida Gomez) produced low-fi intake UI showing recommended lane (Reserved / Flex / Hybrid), suggested GPU family, and a confidence score. Design flagged potential confusion around 'burst credits' terminology.

2026-03-08 - Trade-off meeting: two paths surfaced: (A) conservative mapping that favors higher GPU class for low-latency SLOs (higher cost, fewer SLA misses) vs (B) cost-first mapping with aggressive fallback policies. Decision: prototype both and measure tradeoffs on historical request sampling.
2026-03-09 - Added dependency on ENG-58122 (autoscaling policy v2) for integrating burst window enforcement. Capacity Ops requested clear TTLs for burst credits and failover rollbacks.

2026-03-11 - Implemented scoring simulation on historical dataset (N=420 enterprise intakes). Early results: conservative mapping reduced projected SLA violation risk from 8.2% to 1.9% at 1.7x cost multiplier.
2026-03-12 - Legal reviewed compliance constraints for on-prem GPU families. No blocking issues but flagged contractual language for reserved throughput guarantees.
2026-03-13 - Draft runbook added to Confluence. Action: ENG to wire recommended GPU family and reserved throughput to onboarding API (PR linked).

2026-03-14 - In Review: Product asked for an explicit 'explainability' field in intake UI showing why a GPU family was chosen (e.g., expected CPU/GPU memory footprint, KV cache hit assumptions). Engineering to estimate implementation effort.
Next steps - Schedule pilot with three customers across industries (fintech, NLP platform, internal Redwood trial). Capacity Ops to allocate warm pool for one pilot to validate warm-up times.
notes: Scoring inputs recommended: requested P99 latency, expected concurrent sessions, model tokenization length distribution, preferred model families, compliance flags, cost sensitivity label.

GPU class mapping heuristics: map P99 < 150ms to A100/H100 family with 99% confidence band, P99 150-400ms to A10/A30/RTX alternatives with burst credit allowances, otherwise recommend shared reserved lanes.

Burst policy: define a 5-minute burst window with configurable burst credits based on reserved throughput ratio and historical peak factors. Conservatively cap burst at 2x reserved unless customer purchases burst add-on.
Fallback ladder: recommended GPU variant -> compatible quantized variant -> lower-priority regional pool -> queued degraded response mode with grace messages to customer app.
Operational constraints: autoscaler cooldown, warm pool pre-warm time, billing implications for reserved vs burst usage must be surfaced to sales and legal teams.
